units.text: CONVERGENCE AND STRONG SUMMABILITY OF THE TWO-DIMENSIONAL VILENKIN-FOURIER SERIES
Introduction

The definitions and notations used in this introduction can be found in our next Section. It is known [16, p. 125] that the two-dimensional Vilenkin systems are not Schauder bases in L 1 (G 2 m ) . Moreover, (see [1] and [25]) there exists a function f ∈ H p (G 2 m ) , such that the corresponding partial sums are not bounded in L p (G 2 m ) , for all 0 < p ≤ 1. However, Weisz [47] proved that if α ≥ 0, 0 < p ≤ 1 and f ∈ H p (G 2 m ) , then there exists an absolute constant c p , depending only on p, such that where [p] denotes the integer part of p. Moreover, in [36] it was proved that the rate of sequence (kl) 2−p (0 < p < 1) in inequality (1) can not be improved, which gives sharpness for α > 0.
In the case when α = 0 and 0 < p ≤ 1 it follows that if f ∈ H p (G 2 m ) , then there exists an absolute constant c, such that (2) sup

For the two-dimensional Walsh-Fourier series Goginava and Gogoladze [14] for p = 1 and Tephnadze [32] for 0 < p < 1 generalized inequality (2) and proved that there exists an absolute constant c p , depending only on p, such that for all f ∈ H p (G 2 m ), where [p] denotes integer part of p. Moreover, in [32] and [33] there were proved that the sequence 1/k 3−2p log 2[p] (k + 1) : k ∈ N in inequality (3) is sharp.

Concerning approximation properties of Fourier series in the classical and real Hardy spaces only few results are known. We refer to the papers by Oswald [23], Kryakin and Trebels [17], Storoienko [30], [31]. The main aim of this paper is to generalize inequality (1) for bounded Vilenkin systems. We also prove that the sequence (kl) 2−p in inequality (1) can not be improved. Moreover, we find necessary and sufficient conditions for modulus of continuity of the two-dimensional Vilenkin-Fourier series, which provide convergence of partial sums in H p (G 2 m ) norm. This paper is organized as follows: in order not to disturb our discussions later on some definitions and notations and some important propositions are presented in Section 2. The main results with proofs can be found in Section 3. Moreover, in Section 4 we will state some interesting open problems and conjectures of this research area. Define the group G m as the complete direct product of the groups Z m i with the product of the discrete topologies of Z m j 's.

Next, we introduce on G 2 m an orthonormal system which is called the Vilenkin system. At first, we define the complex-valued function r k (x) : G m → C, the generalized Rademacher functions by

Now, define the Vilenkin system ψ := (ψ n : n ∈ N) on G m as:

We define the two-dimesional Vilenkin system as a kronecker product of two Vilenkin systems. The Vilenkin system is orthonormal and complete in L 2 (G 2 m ) (for details see [1] and [42]). Specifically, we call this system the Walsh-Paley system, when m ≡ 2.
The rectangular partial sum of the 2-dimensional Vilenkin-Fourier series of function f ∈ L 2 (G 2 m ) is defined as follows:
S M,N f (x, y) := M −1 i=0 N −1 j=0 f (i, j) ψ i (x) ψ j (y) ,
where the numbers
f (i, j) = G 2 m f (x, y)ψ i (x)ψ j (y) dµ (x) dµ (y)
is said to be the (i, j)-th Vilenkin-Fourier coefficient of the function f.
